findings.message:
Resolution type depends on the metadata source, and the sweep test cannot detect it

JFIF-sourced values are Integer (`test.jpg` gives `[72, 72]`). EXIF-sourced values are Float, for JPEG as well as TIFF. `test2.jpg` has no JFIF segment and its EXIF tag is 72/1, so it returns `[72.0, 72.0]`. The PR note says only TIFF is Float, which is wrong for JPEG EXIF. The sweep compares with `assert_equal` ([`test/test.rb:128-131`](https://github.com/sdsykes/fastimage/blob/8fc7cd32904240c2c841e70aef2ba5c3bb659ffd/test/test.rb#L128-L131)), and `72 == 72.0`, so a type change in either direction still passes. Settle the contract first, either by converting whole-number EXIF values or by documenting that EXIF-derived values are Float. Then compare types in the test, for example `assert_equal info[2].inspect, res.inspect`.

`resolution_units` refetches the image whenever there is no resolution

`@resolution` is set only on success. On a miss, `parse_packets` raises `CannotParseImage`, `fetch` swallows it, and `defined?(@resolution)` stays false. So `fi.resolution` followed by `fi.resolution_units` on a GIF, WebP, SVG, or a PNG without pHYs issues a second full HTTP GET. `size` and `animated` already memoize only on success, but `resolution_units` is new and makes the repeat fetch the normal path. Fix: record the miss, for example `@resolution ||= nil` after the `fetch` line in `#resolution`.

Short JPEG segment lengths raise an uncaught NoMethodError from `FastImage.resolution`

`read_int - 2` is negative for length fields 0 or 1. `FiberStream#read` with a negative count returns nil ([`fiber_stream.rb:30`](https://github.com/sdsykes/fastimage/blob/8fc7cd32904240c2c841e70aef2ba5c3bb659ffd/lib/fastimage/fastimage_parsing/fiber_stream.rb#L30)), so `data[0, 5]` or `data[7].ord` raises NoMethodError. A JFIF body shorter than 9 bytes fails at `data[8, 4]`. `fetch` rescues only fetch errors and `CannotParseImage` ([`fastimage.rb:292-298`](https://github.com/sdsykes/fastimage/blob/8fc7cd32904240c2c841e70aef2ba5c3bb659ffd/lib/fastimage/fastimage.rb#L292-L298)), so the error escapes even without `raise_on_failure`. That contradicts the README's "returns nil if it encounters an error." The existing `dimensions` APP1 branch ([`jpeg.rb:89-91`](https://github.com/sdsykes/fastimage/blob/8fc7cd32904240c2c841e70aef2ba5c3bb659ffd/lib/fastimage/fastimage_parsing/jpeg.rb#L89-L91)) has the same unguarded read, so `size` is exposed too, but that predates this change. Fix: raise `CannotParseImage` when `length < 0`, and check the body length before indexing.

TIFF/EXIF rationals located before the IFD are silently dropped

`parse_exif` skips to the IFD, and the stream cannot rewind. A rational whose offset is behind the current position hits `next if skip_amount < 0`, so that tag is lost. If X or Y is lost, `tiff.rb:18` returns nil. Two tags sharing one offset produce the same result for the second tag. TIFF 6.0 allows value offsets anywhere in the file. No fixture exercises this layout; all shipped TIFF and EXIF fixtures put the rationals after the IFD. I did not establish how common this layout is in real writers. Fix: buffer a bounded header-to-IFD window when `parse_resolution` is set, or document the limitation.

Untested branches: `:centimeters` and the BMP zero-PPM nil return

Every EXIF fixture uses unit 2 (inches), and the JFIF fixtures use units 0 and 1, so no test reaches a centimeters mapping. Changing `:centimeters` to `:inches` would still pass. `test_coreheader.bmp` is the only expected nil, and it returns at the header-size check (`bmp.rb:20`), so the zero-PPM return has no fixture. Add small synthetic IO inputs: a JFIF APP0 with units=2, and a 54-byte BMP with zero PPM.

The JPEG `resolution` method duplicates the `dimensions` marker walk

The two state machines share a skeleton and an APP1-to-Exif unwrap, and they already differ in policy: `dimensions` keeps only the first APP1, while `resolution` continues until one carries resolution. Marker-handling fixes will have to land twice. Extract the APP1 step into a helper and document the intended difference.

EXIF unit mapping and tag dispatch are split across three places with different defaults

`TAG_RESOLUTION_UNIT` is read only in the SHORT branch, so a LONG-typed unit is ignored and falls back to inches. The EXIF unit switch is written twice, in jpeg.rb and tiff.rb. Unknown codes map to `:no_units` for JFIF but to `:inches` for EXIF. One helper with one explicit default would remove the drift.

`.idea` is per-developer IDE state and is not part of resolution support. Drop it from this PR or move it to a global excludes file.
